newsitem.title: USA: Exigent sees loss on IPO expenses.
newsitem.headline: Exigent sees loss on IPO expenses.

text.p: Exigent International Inc said on Wednesday it expects to report a net loss in excess of $400,000 for the year ended January 31, due primarily to more than $1 million in non-recurring expenses associated with becoming a publicly traded company.

A reduction in revenues in connection with one of the company's multi-year commercial contracts also hurt fiscal 1997 earnings, it said. The customer extended the schedule for commercial deployment under the contract. Contractual coverage is pending negotiation.

The company said it expects to report revenues rose nearly 20 percent in the latest year to about $30 million from about $25.3 million in fiscal 1996. Exigent earned $1,131,741, or $0.25 per share on a pro forma basis, in fiscal 1996.

About $325,000 of the IPO expenses represented cash expenditures, the company said. The remaining amount of the charge, some $675,000, was a non-cash payment in the form of stock required to be expensed by generally accepted accounting principles. This non-cash expense is equal to the difference of the appraised value of the shares issued by the company and the price it actually received for them.

Exigent said management declined to give specific projections for fiscal 1998, but believes revenues will continue to increase and anticipates that net income as a percentage of revenues should be more consistent with years prior to fiscal 1997.
